name: Saṃyama
method_summary: Saṃyama is concentration, meditation and samādhi on one object (3.4). The text says it is applied to the stage next after the one mastered, not skipping to far stages (bhāṣya 3.6), and gives the objects on which saṃyama is said to bring various results (3.16 onward). The text gives no procedure beyond this.
prerequisites: mastery of the lower stage before the next (bhāṣya 3.6)
signs_of_progress: the light of insight (3.5), clearer as saṃyama takes firm footing (bhāṣya 3.5)

warnings.text: na hy ajitādharabhūmir anantarabhūmiṃ vilaṅghya prāntabhūmiṣu saṃyamaṃ labhate

name: Dhāraṇā (concentration)
method_summary: The binding of the mind to a place (3.1); the bhāṣya names as places the navel wheel, the lotus of the heart, the light in the head, the tip of the nose, the tip of the tongue, or an external object, the mind being bound by its activity alone.

name: Samādhi (in the Vibhūti-pāda account)
method_summary: That same meditation, shining as the object alone and as if empty of its own form (3.3). Among the states named in this part: samādhi, in which the perceptions of 3.36 are obstacles (3.37); dharma-megha samādhi (4.29).

name: Declining the invitations of the high stations (YS 3.51)
method_summary: As the bhāṣya on 3.51 states it: when gods of high stations invite the yogin who has realised the madhumatī stage, he reflects on the faults of attachment (that he has obtained the lamp of yoga in the darkness of saṃsāra and would be deceived by a mirage of sense-objects), dismisses the offers as dream-like, and cultivates samādhi; having no attachment he also feels no pride, for pride would make him think himself secure, and heedlessness watching for a gap would stir the afflictions again.

name: Cessation of vāsanās and saṃskāras as the text states it
method_summary: The text states that vāsanās are held together by cause, fruit, support and object and cease when these are absent (4.11); that the earlier saṃskāra whose seed is burnt by the fire of knowledge no longer yields cognition (bhāṣya 4.28); and that with the destruction of the seeds of saṃskāra no other cognitions arise and dharma-megha follows (4.29). It gives no separate method here.
